title: Converting Tub To Walk In Shower: A Look At The Process
imageAlt: Walk-in tub with glass doors, grab bars and marble-look walls
excerpt: For many homeowners, traditional bathtubs no longer meet their needs. Whether you're looking to improve safety, enhance accessibility, or simply modernize your bathroom, converting a tub to a walk-in shower is a practical and stylish solution. This guide outlines the…
body: For many homeowners, traditional bathtubs no longer meet their needs. Whether you're looking to improve safety, enhance accessibility, or simply modernize your bathroom, converting a tub to a walk-in shower is a practical and stylish solution. This guide outlines the process from first call to first shower.

A local specialist measures your existing tub alcove, checks the plumbing and talks through how you use the bathroom today. You'll see wall patterns, bases, doors and safety accessories, and get clear pricing before anything is scheduled.

On installation day the crew protects your floors, disconnects the plumbing and removes the old tub and surround. Any damaged subfloor or wall board is repaired so the new shower sits on a solid, level surface.
A low-threshold base is set in place, the drain is connected and custom-fitted wall panels go up. Grab bars, a shower seat, a hand-held wand and shelves are added where they work best for you.
Most conversions are completed in as little as one day. Before the crew leaves, they walk you through care and maintenance and make sure everything is exactly as planned.

title: Aging In Place Remodeling: A Complete Guide
imageAlt: Close-up of a shower with wood-grain wall panels and a chrome hand shower bracket
excerpt: Aging in place is a concept that resonates with many seniors. It's about staying in the comfort of your own home as you age, surrounded by familiar surroundings and cherished memories. However, for this dream to be safe and practical…
body: Aging in place is a concept that resonates with many seniors. It's about staying in the comfort of your own home as you age, surrounded by familiar surroundings and cherished memories. However, for this dream to be safe and practical, the home often needs a few thoughtful changes.

The bathroom is where most falls at home happen. A low-threshold walk-in shower or a walk-in tub with a door removes the need to step over a high tub wall, while grab bars, seating and non-slip surfaces add everyday security.
Stairs become harder over time. A stair lift fits straight or curved staircases, and a through-floor home elevator can connect levels without a large footprint or a machine room.

Brighter lighting, lever-style handles, wider doorways and easy-to-reach storage all make daily life simpler. A good aging-in-place plan looks at the whole home and prioritizes the changes that matter most for you.
Caliber Home Solutions offers free in-home consultations to help you build that plan.

title: Elevator Lifts for Homes: Making the Right Choice
imageAlt: Smiling woman using a compact residential elevator in a bright home
excerpt: Finding the perfect elevator lift for your home can be a challenging decision. Homeowners often seek elevator lifts for homes that improve mobility and accessibility while maintaining the aesthetic appeal of their living spaces. Whether you're planning to age in…
body: Finding the perfect elevator lift for your home can be a challenging decision. Homeowners often seek elevator lifts for homes that improve mobility and accessibility while maintaining the aesthetic appeal of their living spaces.

Through-floor elevators, such as Stiltz home lifts, travel between two floors without a shaft or machine room and plug into a standard outlet. Shaft-based residential elevators can serve more floors and larger cabins but need more construction.
Consider who will ride and how. Some lifts carry one or two people; larger models accommodate three people or a wheelchair user and a companion.
A specialist will look at floor plans, ceiling heights and traffic flow to find a spot that is convenient and blends with your décor, often in a corner of a living room, hallway or closet.
Book a free consultation and we'll help you compare options side by side.

title: Choosing the Right Walk in Tub with Shower for Your Bathroom
imageAlt: Walk-in tub with shower and glass enclosure
excerpt: When it comes to enhancing safety and comfort in your bathroom, few upgrades are as transformative as a walk-in tub with shower. Combining accessibility, therapeutic benefits, and modern design, these tubs are a perfect solution for homeowners who want to…
body: When it comes to enhancing safety and comfort in your bathroom, few upgrades are as transformative as a walk-in tub with shower. Combining accessibility, therapeutic benefits, and modern design, these tubs suit homeowners who want both a relaxing soak and a quick daily shower.
Inward- and outward-opening doors each have advantages. Look for a low step-in height and a door that opens fully so you can enter and exit without twisting.
Air jets, hydrotherapy jets, heated seats and chromatherapy turn bath time into a spa experience. Choose the features you'll actually use.
A hand-held wand on a slide bar, a fixed rain head and a glass enclosure let the tub double as a comfortable shower on busy days.
Our consultants can show you Jacuzzi® Bath Remodel walk-in tubs in person during a free visit.

title: Benefits Of A Walk In Shower With Seat
imageAlt: Black rain shower head spraying water
excerpt: Upgrading your bathroom can be an exciting project, but it's also an opportunity to enhance your home's comfort, safety, and style. One bathroom upgrade that ticks all three boxes is a walk-in shower with a seat. These showers are a…
body: Upgrading your bathroom can be an exciting project, but it's also an opportunity to enhance your home's comfort, safety, and style. One bathroom upgrade that ticks all three boxes is a walk-in shower with a seat.
Sitting while you wash reduces the risk of losing your balance. Combined with grab bars and a slip-resistant base, a seat makes showering safer for everyone.
A built-in or fold-down seat gives you a place to rest, shave or simply relax under warm water.
Modern seats come in teak, solid-surface and wall-mounted fold-down designs that look built for the space rather than added later.

title: Age In Place House Plans That Embrace Aging Gracefully
imageAlt: Man smiling while riding a stair lift on a curved staircase
excerpt: As we move through different phases of life, our needs change, and the way we live and interact with our homes evolves. Finding the right home design becomes especially crucial as we age, and one approach that's been gaining popularity…
body: As we move through different phases of life, our needs change, and the way we live and interact with our homes evolves. Finding the right home design becomes especially crucial as we age, and one approach that's been gaining popularity is planning for aging in place from the start.
A main-floor bedroom, bathroom and laundry mean you never have to rely on stairs for daily essentials.
If your home has more than one level, leave space for a future stair lift or home elevator. Stacked closets make an ideal elevator location.
Curbless or low-threshold showers, blocking for grab bars and wider doorways cost little during construction and pay off for decades.

title: Walk In Shower Ideas For Small Bathrooms
imageAlt: Compact bathroom with a glass-enclosed walk-in bath and shower
excerpt: Designing a small bathroom can feel like a challenge, but a well-planned walk-in shower can dramatically transform the space. Not only does it maximize the available room, but it also creates an open, modern feel that makes even the smallest…
body: Designing a small bathroom can feel like a challenge, but a well-planned walk-in shower can dramatically transform the space. Not only does it maximize the available room, but it also creates an open, modern feel that makes even the smallest bathroom seem larger.
A frameless or semi-frameless clear glass door keeps sight lines open and lets light travel through the room.
Large-format panels with few seams make walls feel calm and continuous, and they are far easier to clean than grout.
Recessed niches and slim corner shelves keep bottles off the floor without taking up space.

title: Residential Elevators And Lifts: A Complete Guide
imageAlt: Glass home elevator in a bright living room
excerpt: As modern homes continue to evolve, one feature that has gained popularity for both convenience and luxury is the residential elevator. Whether you have a multi-level home, live with elderly family members, or simply want to make your space more…
body: As modern homes continue to evolve, one feature that has gained popularity for both convenience and luxury is the residential elevator. Whether you have a multi-level home, live with elderly family members, or simply want to make your space more accessible, there is a lift to fit.
Stair lifts follow your staircase, vertical platform lifts help wheelchair users reach porches and decks, and home elevators move people between floors.
Most stair lifts install in a day. Through-floor elevators typically take a few days, with minimal disruption compared with a traditional shaft elevator.
Price depends on the type of lift, the number of floors and finishes. Ask about current offers and financing during your free consultation.

title: How To Choose The Best Stairlift Company
imageAlt: Woman riding a stair lift while children sit on the stairs
excerpt: Choosing the right stairlift company can be a daunting task. Every year, thousands of families find this task challenging as they seek to improve home accessibility. This article guides you through selecting a reliable stairlift provider, focusing on factors like reputation, customization, and customer…
body: Choosing the right stairlift company can be a daunting task. Every year, thousands of families find this task challenging as they seek to improve home accessibility. Here's what to look for.
Read reviews, ask how long the company has been in business and whether it is an authorized dealer for the brands it sells.
Straight, curved and outdoor stairs all need different solutions. A good provider measures in person and offers options for seats, rails and controls.
Ask about warranties, maintenance and how quickly a local technician can respond if you ever need help.
